thread.title: Asian markets continue to retreat as tech stocks get hit hard - MarketWatch

author: Dow Jones Newswires
title: Asian markets continue to retreat as tech stocks get hit hard - MarketWatch
text:
Published: Nov 21, 2018 6:49 a.m. ET Share
Nikkei nears 1-month low AFP/Getty Images Tsukimi Namiki of Japan gets clocked at the AIBA Women's World Boxing Championships in New Delhi on Tuesday.
By Dow Jones Newswires
Asian stock markets mostly fell early but improved from the worst levels of the day, including a flip to positive territory in Hong Kong, as the region’s trading tracked the drubbing Tuesday for U.S. stocks and oil futures. Both equities and oil markets indicated a Wednesday rebound was in order.
Japan’s Nikkei NIK, -0.35% was down 0.4%, moving close to its lowest point in a month as energy and electronics stocks slid. Oil explorer Inpex 1605, -3.26% was down 3.2% while Sumitomo 8053, -3.17% , which has various natural-resource investments around the world, lost 3.2%. Meanwhile, Olympus 7733, -8.69% dropped 8.7% and Mitsubishi Electric 6503, -2.67% was off 2.7%. Nissan shares 7201, +0.36% reversed a bit of yesterday’s slide following the arrest of CEO Carlos Ghosn .
Hong Kong stocks extended losses initially though the Hang Seng Index HSI, +0.51% closed up 0.5% after dropping more than 1% early on. While tech stocks lagged overall, Tencent 0700, +2.84% gained 2.8% and AAC 2018, +1.85% rose 1.9%. Oil company Cnooc 0883, -2.45% fell 2.5%.
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, +0.21% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite 399106, +0.54% were both up slightly after early weakness. Energy stocks lagged after the latest plunge in oil prices CLF9, +1.78% Tuesday.
Sagging energy stocks also weighed down Australia’s ASX 200 XJO, -0.51% , with Woodside Petroleum WPL, -2.10% down 2% and Santos STO, -4.35% off 4.3%. New Zealand’s benchmark NZ50GR, -0.55% was down slightly.
South Korea’s Kospi SEU, -0.29% declined 0.3%, as Samsung 005930, -1.64% dipped. Singapore’s Strai Times Index STI, +0.39% rose 0.4% while Taiwan’s Taiex Y9999, -0.03% slipped 0.03% as Apple AAPL, +0.44% suppliers Foxconn 2354, -0.97% and Largan Precision 3008, +0.90% fell.
